pages.title: The cardiovascular system ensures blood circulation in the body

blocks.text: The cardiovascular system ensures blood circulation in the body. It is made up of two main parts: The cardiac part represented by the heart. The vascular part represented by the vessels: arteries and veins. These two parts form the circulatory system: The heart is the blood ejection pump The vessels are the blood transporters A system parallel to the circulatory network is the lymphatic system. Introduction to the cardiovascular system The cardiovascular system ensures the circulation of blood throughout the body. It is made up of two main parts: The cardiac part, represented by the heart The vascular part, represented by the vessels: arteries and veins. These two parts make up the circulatory system: The heart is the blood ejection pump The vessels transport the blood. A parallel system to the circulatory network is the lymphatic system. Definition The heart is a hollow muscle divided into four cavities, firm in consistency and red in color. It is the main organ of the circulatory system, and plays the role of a pump that sends blood through the vessels. It is a vital organ.

Definition The heart is a hollow muscle, divided into four chambers, firm in consistency and red in color. It is the main organ of the circulatory system, acting as a pump that sends blood to the blood vessels. It is a vital organ. .

General Situation The heart is located in the thorax, between the two lungs, above the diaphragm and occupies the anterior mediastinum. Shape and orientation The heart is shaped like a triangular pyramid with three faces, three edges, a base, and an apex or point of the heart. Its axis is oriented downwards, to the left and outwards. Color: reddish. Consistency: firm. Length: 12cm. Weight: 250 to 300 g. Capacity: 800 cm3. Heart rate 60 to 80 beats/minute

blocks.text: INTERIOR CONFIGURATION OF THE HEART

The internal configuration of the heart refers to the main characteristics visible from the inside of the heart. The heart is divided by partitions or septa into four right and left chambers. Right atrium and ventricle form the right heart Left atrium and ventricle form the left heart The atriums communicate with the ventricles through the atrioventricular orifices equipped with valves. The ventricles communicate with the aorta and the pulmonary artery through arterial orifices equipped with sigmoid valves.

pages.title: The cardiovascular system ensures blood circulation in the body

blocks.text: Each ventricle is divided into two functional parts: a filling chamber and an outflow chamber. The partitions or septa are three in number; atrioventricular, interatrial, and interventricular. These are membranes made up of a muscular part and a membranous part. The walls of the ventricles and atriums are different. The ventricles have thick walls, and have muscular projections called fleshy columns which are of three orders:

items: Fleshy columns of 1st order or, papillary muscles or pillars, the free end of the column is connected to the atrioventicular valves by the chordae tendineae.

2nd order fleshy columns or trabeculae, are flattened; they are inserted into the ventricle at their ends and are free at the middle part. (Example of the ensiform or septomarginal strip of the right ventricle).
3rd order fleshy columns have simple muscular projections adhering to the wall.

The chordae tendineae are fibrous cords which connect the pillars to the free edges of the atrioventricular valves. The walls of the atriums are thinner and smooth, have a few fleshy columns of 2nd and 3rd

blocks.text: order and small muscles called pectineus muscles.

pages.title: These three walls present the fleshy columns of 1st, 2nd and 3rd order

blocks.text: These three walls present the fleshy columns of 1st, 2nd and 3rd order. The base: has two orifices:

items: The right atrioventricular orifice: communicates the atrium and the ventricle (right). It is circular, with a circumference measuring on average 120 mm, equipped with a tricuspid valve having 3 valves; anterior, inferior and internal. Each valve receives tendinous cords stretched from a fleshy column of the 1st order of the wall which corresponds to it.

The arterial orifice: This is the orifice of the pulmonary artery. It is circular with 3 sigmoid valves: one anterior and two posterior right and left. The summit: presents numerous fleshy columns of 2nd and 3rd order.

blocks.text: 2- Right atrium: cubic in shape with six walls:

items: Anterior wall: corresponds to the right atrioventricular orifice.
External or lateral wall: presents fleshy columns of 3rd order. - posterior wall: presents between the 02 orifices of the two upper and lower vena cavae a projection: the Lower tubercle.

Internal or medial wall: made up of the inter-atrial septum, it presents a rounded depressure, the fossa ovale, limited by a protruding ring, the Vieussens ring or limbus (remnant of the Botal canal which has closed).
Superior wall: presents the orifice of the superior vena cava.

Lower wall: has two openings; the orifice of the inferior vena cava which presents the Eustachian valve and the orifice of the coronary sinus equipped with the valve of Thebesius. A- THE LEFT HEART 1-Left ventricle, conical, with two external and internal walls, a base and an apex The walls
The internal wall responds to the interventricular septum.
The outer wall responds to the left lateral aspect of the heart. Both the inner and outer walls have fleshy columns. The base has two orifices:

Left atrioventricular orifice: circular, with a circumference measuring on average 110 mm, equipped with a mitral valve with two valves: internal, large or right and external, small or left. The chordae tendineae of the anterior and posterior pillars end on its valves.
Aortic orifice: it is the orifice of the aorta, includes 3 sigmoid valves: 02 anterior right and left and one posterior.

blocks.text: Abstract The heart, the central organ of the circulatory system, is a hollow red muscle that contracts rhythmically and involuntarily. It is intra-thoracic, occupying the middle mediastinum and remaining on the diaphragm. Its long axis is oblique forward, downwards and to the left, so that its apex is situated to the left and its base to the right. It has the shape of a triangular pyramid with three faces, one of which remains on the flat diaphragm and is known as the diaphragm. The second, facing the lung, is convex convex, known as the left lateral. A third anterior, facing the costal grill, is called sternocostal. Its outer surface is criss-crossed by grooves through which the arteries of the heart run, covered by fatty tissuee. The internal configuration of the heart consists of four chambers, valves, and associated structures that regulate blood flow:

items: Chambers: o Right atrium: Receives deoxygenated blood from the body. o Right ventricle: Pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs. o Left atrium: Receives oxygenated blood from the lungs. o Left ventricle: Pumps oxygenated blood to the body.

Valves: o Tricuspid valve: Between right atrium and ventricle. o Pulmonary valve: Between right ventricle and pulmonary artery. o Mitral valve: Between left atrium and ventricle. o Aortic valve: Between left ventricle and aorta.
Septum: Divides the heart into left and right sides: o Interatrial septum: Between atria. o Interventricular septum: Between ventricles References
